# QS-CFW-1140-78 Quality specification - axle hub CFW-1140-78 (4140)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-1140-78

Scope
This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of the axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) forged from 4140 material in Plant P1. It defines the acceptance criteria for mechanical condition and dimensional features important to fit, function, and downstream machining. This document is mandatory for all production lots and for any rework intended to return parts to saleable condition.

Background and rationale
Axle hubs for heavy equipment require controlled hardness for wear resistance and sufficient toughness for fatigue performance. The bore fits critical mating components; therefore, dimensional tolerance is controlled tightly to ensure consistent assembly and to minimize scrap during finish machining. The maximum forging weight is limited to ensure die life and press capacity, and to control cooling and microstructure uniformity. The specific values in this document reflect validated process capability and incoming material characteristics for the 4140 grade used in Plant P1.

Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|
| Material | 4140 per procurement specification | Certificate required with each lot |
| Hardness (through radial section after heat treatment) | The hardness range for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) is 27-32 HRC. | Measured values must fall within the range across inspection locations; statistical trending required for outliers |
| Bore diameter | Machined bore tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) is ±0.08 mm. |
| Forging weight | Casting/forging process control | The maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) is 93.3 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of laps, seams, and forging cracks | Visual and penetrant inspection per Inspection Method below |
| Documentation | Material certificate, process travelers, inspection records | Must be retained per Records to keep below |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspections are performed on a sampling basis defined by the plant quality plan; however, the inspection methods below represent the mandatory tests and measurements that must be performed on initial production pieces, after process changes, and for any suspect lot.

Hardness measurement
- Hardness testing shall be performed on production parts after final heat treatment and prior to finish machining operations. Portable or bench Rockwell testers selected must be calibrated and traceable to calibration standards. Test locations should represent radial distribution and include the bore region and spoke/web area to detect local variations.
- Acceptance criteria are based on the hardness range above. If any measured point falls outside the specified range, follow the Nonconformance handling section.

Bore diameter inspection
- Bore diameter shall be inspected using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measurement equipment capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Measurements must be taken at multiple axial locations and averaged for reporting.
- Report results in the inspection record and mark parts only when within the tolerance specified above. For assemblies where rework is necessary, refer to Nonconformance handling.

Visual and non-destructive examination
- Perform a visual inspection under adequate illumination to identify surface defects. Penetrant inspection shall be used where surface-breaking discontinuities are suspected or where required by process travelers.
- Any discontinuity identified that could affect fit, function, or fatigue life must be evaluated per Nonconformance handling.

Sampling and statistical trending
- Document all inspection results in the lot inspection report. Track hardness and bore measurements for trending. Continuous drift or repeated border-line results should trigger process review even if individual parts meet the literal acceptance criteria.

Calibration and equipment
- All measurement tools used for hardness and bore inspection must be calibrated against traceable standards. Records of calibration must be available in the inspection folder for each lot.

Inspection records and examples
- Example entry: Lot identifier, part number CFW-1140-78, measured hardness locations and values, bore location measurements with mean and deviation, inspector initials, equipment ID, and calibration reference. Use the plant inspection form for format consistency.
- Records to keep: material certificates, heat-treatment records, inspection reports, calibration certificates, process travelers, and nonconformance reports. Retain according to Plant P1 retention policy.

Nonconformance handling
Detection and immediate action
- If a part fails to meet any requirement in the Requirements table, the part must be segregated and labeled as nonconforming. Notify quality lead and document the nonconformance in the lot file.

Disposition options
- Conditional rework: Parts failing bore tolerance may be eligible for machining rework if adequate stock and design allow, and if rework will restore the part to full conformance. Rework must be documented and approved by engineering and quality prior to execution.
- Material or process failure: Parts that exhibit hardness outside the specified range, or any crack-like discontinuity, are considered suspect for structural performance and may require full scrap or metallurgical investigation. Do not return parts that fail hardness limits to service without a documented engineering disposition.
- Root cause and corrective action: For any repeated nonconformance, initiate a root cause analysis and corrective action plan. Document findings and corrective measures in the lot file.

Records and reporting
- The lot nonconformance report shall include: description of nonconformance, affected part(s) identified as CFW-1140-78, inspection data demonstrating failure, proposed disposition, and final approval by authorized personnel. Maintain these records with the inspection records described above.

Examples and clarifications
- Example of a permitted action: If a bore measurement is outside the ±0.08 mm. tolerance but machining stock is available and engineering approves, rework to required dimension is allowed with documented sign-off.
- Example of prohibited action: Cooling or tempering adjustments intended to alter hardness post-final inspection without engineering approval are not permitted. Any attempt to alter heat-treatment outcomes must follow a documented process-change procedure and be requalified.

End of document.
